key_insight: An inexact SVRG method improves first-order oracle complexity for constrained convex finite-sum optimization while guaranteeing constraint violation at most ε and expected optimality gap at most ε.
engineering_relevance: The method targets applications with hard constraints and may be especially useful when constraint gradients and cone projections are cheaper than objective gradients.
method: Use inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient updates.
Target ε-surely feasible stochastic optimal solutions, not merely feasibility in expectation.
For a single objective function, specialize to a deterministic first-order method for convex conic optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved theoretical complexity bounds and preliminary numerical results, but provides no benchmark details or quantitative outcomes.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on the relative costs of objective gradients, constraint gradients, and cone projections.
paper_title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
